chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Muʿādhī, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Ṭayālisī, from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Is a man held accountable through his close kinsman when he commits an offense?” He said to me: “Yes, unless he has brought him out to the assembly of his people and dissociated himself from his offense and his inheritance.”

key_terms.حَمِيمِهِ: his close kinsman or intimate relative
key_terms.مِيرَاثِهِ: his inheritance rights or inheritance connection
key_terms.نَادِي قَوْمِهِ: the public assembly of his people

ai.seo_question: Can a person be held liable for the crime of a close relative in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning liability connected to a close kinsman who commits an offense. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that such liability applies unless a public dissociation is made before the offender's people, including disavowal of both the offense and inheritance ties.
